transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Ever since the wreck, I just can’t think straight long enough to do my work or make simple decisions, it’s like my mind keeps stalling out. I’m a self-employed tax preparer, and right now I can’t even get through basic client files without getting completely overwhelmed and stuck.
Since the accident, do you have unwanted memories, nightmares, or feel like you’re reliving it? Or is it mainly headaches, dizziness, and trouble concentrating without those trauma memories?

I don't have headaches or dizziness, but the trouble concentrating and my mind blanking out is a massive issue. I don't really have nightmares, but I actually have a frustrating blank spot in my memory for the minutes right after the impact, even though I can picture the crash itself clearly.
Right after the crash, did you lose consciousness or feel dazed/confused, and if so, for about how long? Also, did a doctor tell you that you had a concussion or any brain injury?

I honestly don't know if I lost consciousness or was just dazed, because I have a total blank spot between seeing the headlights and suddenly being outside on the stretcher. The ER discharged me that same night with only minor physical injuries, and they didn't say anything about a concussion or brain injury.

Since the accident, have you been unusually sensitive to noise or light, getting fatigued easily, or feeling more irritable or emotionally upset than before? Or is it mainly just the thinking and memory problems without those other symptoms?

It’s definitely not just the thinking problems, though I don't have light sensitivity or fatigue. I’ve become extremely sensitive to sudden noises, jumping out of my chair and shaking if my wife walks in unexpectedly or a car door slams outside. I also feel constantly on edge, scanning my surroundings, and instead of feeling irritable, I just feel completely flat and disconnected from any positive emotions.
Since the crash, do you find yourself avoiding reminders of it, like driving, the accident site, conversations about it, or thoughts about what happened? If so, what kinds of things do you avoid?

I haven't really been actively avoiding those situations or reminders. But when I do ride in a car or go near that intersection, things just feel very strange and disconnected, like I'm watching a movie of my own life.

When you’re near that intersection or hear sudden noises, do you ever get vivid unwanted images or feel for a moment like the crash is happening again? Or is it mainly feeling detached and on edge without reliving it?

I don't actually relive the crash or get flashbacks, it's more that I feel completely detached and highly on edge. When I'm near that intersection, everything feels weirdly fake and distant, like I'm watching a movie of my life from outside my body. And sudden noises just make me jump out of my skin and leave me shaking, rather than making me feel like the accident is happening again.
How long has it been since the accident, and have these symptoms lasted more than one month? Did they start right away after the crash or begin later?

The accident happened exactly two weeks ago, and all of these symptoms started immediately after the crash. Since it's only been two weeks, they haven't lasted for more than a month, but they have been constant every day since the wreck.

Since the crash, have there been moments when you felt unable to remember important parts of what happened beyond just the minutes right after the impact? Also, do you ever feel emotionally numb or like you are not fully aware of what’s going on around you?

No, that blank space between seeing the headlights and being on the stretcher is the only part of the accident I can't remember. But I absolutely feel emotionally numb; when my wife shares good news, it just bounces off me and I feel completely flat and disconnected. There are also times when everything around me feels fake and far away, like I'm floating behind my own body watching a movie of my life.

Since the crash, have there been periods when you felt dazed or less aware of your surroundings, like things were in a fog or you were on autopilot? If so, does that happen even when you’re not near reminders of the accident?

Yes, I definitely have those moments where everything feels fake and far away, like I'm floating a few feet behind myself watching a movie of my own life. It mostly happens when I'm riding in a car or walking past the intersection where the crash occurred, rather than just out of nowhere. Outside of those specific reminders, my mind usually just blanks out or stalls rather than feeling that disconnected.
